partial_progress.details: Phases 1-5 of 11 complete and committed cleanly (depth-first, one phase closed before the next opened). Phases 1-2 landed the independently-landable Gate 8 finding-extraction fix and its 13-site generalization. Phase 3 built an idle-guarded cost-measurement harness and captured a clean 23-gate cost table. Phase 4 introduced the declarative gate registry and migrated gates 1-8 with proven byte-identical output. Phase 5 completed the migration (gates 9-23 wrapped as gateN_run() functions, one shared execution loop), added --max-cost cost-class selection, and re-verified all five deploy_findings_snapshot callers green. Pausing at this clean phase boundary rather than opening Phase 6 (uniform bounded timeouts per gate and per suite, requiring a deliberately-stalled fixture and a full-battery re-run) given the real-world time already spent on this dispatch (multiple multi-minute background waits for idle-load windows, a full-battery measurement, and six existing regression suites re-run for confirmation).

artifacts.summary: Partial implementation summary covering phases 1-5: Gate 8 extraction fix and generalization, idle cost re-baseline, gate-registry migration of gates 1-8, and completion of the migration (gates 9-23) with cost-class selection.

completion_data.completion_summary: Completed phases 1-5 of the 11-phase gate-framework refactor: fixed and generalized the Gate 8/14-site unanchored finding-extraction defect, built an idle-load-guarded cost-measurement harness with a clean 23-gate cost table, and migrated all 23 gates onto a declarative registry (Phase 4: gates 1-8; Phase 5: gates 9-23), adding --max-cost selection and re-verifying all five deploy_findings_snapshot callers green. Every gate now runs through one shared execution loop; no inline gate block remains at verify-deploy.sh's top level. Phases 6-11 (timeouts, concurrency scheduler, shellcheck parallelization, shared corpus enumeration, run-all.sh default flip, final redeploy and measured verification) remain.

memory_candidates.content: IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c ... silently collapses a genuinely EMPTY field between two tabs in a TSV row, shifting every later column by one -- bash classifies tab as an IFS-whitespace character even when it is IFS's sole member, so consecutive-delimiter sequences (which an empty field produces) are treated the same as leading/trailing whitespace stripping and silently merged. This is NOT specific to tab -- any IFS value consisting entirely of whitespace-class characters (space, tab, newline) has this behavior; only a non-whitespace single-char delimiter (comma, pipe) reliably preserves empty fields under plain `read`. Fix: use a placeholder token (e.g. '-') for an intentionally-empty TSV field, and normalize it back to empty string after the read, rather than emitting a bare empty field between two tabs.

When extracting N copy-pasted bash blocks into named functions for a declarative-dispatch refactor, inserting the function DEFINITIONS section immediately adjacent to (just before) the blocks' own original textual position -- rather than relocating them to a logically-organized-but-distant new location (e.g. top of file) -- keeps the diff minimal and easy to review: git's diff recognizes the largely-unchanged body text as context rather than wholesale delete+add, even though the surrounding control flow (an if/fi wrapper replaced by a loop) did change. This made an 8-gate, ~340-line extraction show as a ~55-line diff instead of a full-file rewrite, and made a byte-identical-output verification trivial to trust by inspection as well as by diff.

When writing a line-based bash-block-depth tracker (e.g. to mechanically locate and wrap N copy-pasted if/fi blocks for a refactor), matching closing keywords (`fi`/`done`/`esac`) by EXACT string equality on the stripped line (`stripped == 'done'`) silently breaks on a line like `done < <(some_command)` -- a `done` immediately followed by a redirection/process-substitution on the SAME line. The exact-equality check never matches, the depth counter never decrements for that block, and the tracker silently overshoots into unrelated later code before finally matching some much-later `fi`/`done`, producing a corrupted span with no error raised. Fix: match on a leading-word regex (`^done\b`, `^fi\b`, `^esac\b`) instead of exact equality, so trailing content on the same closing-keyword line doesn't defeat the match.
